title: Authors and Books
statement:
Create two related tables and protect their data with constraints.

The database starts empty. Create `authors` with these columns and constraints:

- `id`: `integer` identity column, the primary key
- `name`: `text`, required and unique
- `country`: `text`, optional

Then create `books`:

- `id`: `integer` identity column, the primary key
- `title`: `text`, required
- `author_id`: `integer`, required, a foreign key to `authors(id)`
- `published_year`: `integer`, optional, with a check that it is at least 1450

Add no other constraints and give them no names, so PostgreSQL names them itself. The starter already inserts three authors and five books, lists each book with its author's name ordered by `title`, and then lists every constraint on the two tables from the `pg_constraint` catalog. In its `type` column, `p` is a primary key, `f` a foreign key, `u` unique, `n` not null, and `c` a check.

```text
---------------------------+-------------------+----------------

 Kindred                   | Octavia E. Butler |           1979

 The Left Hand of Darkness | Ursula K. Le Guin |           1969
 Things Fall Apart         | Chinua Achebe     |           1958
(5 rows)

 table_name |      constraint_name       | type
------------+----------------------------+------
 authors    | authors_id_not_null        | n
 authors    | authors_name_key           | u
 authors    | authors_name_not_null      | n
 authors    | authors_pkey               | p
 books      | books_author_id_fkey       | f
 books      | books_author_id_not_null   | n
 books      | books_id_not_null          | n
 books      | books_pkey                 | p
 books      | books_published_year_check | c
 books      | books_title_not_null       | n
(10 rows)
```

`REFERENCES authors (id)` after a column's type makes it a foreign key.
`CHECK (published_year >= 1450)` rejects any row whose year is too early.

sql.solution:
CREATE TABLE authors (
  id integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  country text
);

CREATE TABLE books (
  id integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  title text NOT NULL,
  author_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES authors (id),
  published_year integer CHECK (published_year >= 1450)
);

INSERT INTO authors (name, country) VALUES
  ('Ursula K. Le Guin', 'United States'),
  ('Chinua Achebe', 'Nigeria'),
  ('Octavia E. Butler', 'United States');

INSERT INTO books (title, author_id, published_year) VALUES
  ('The Left Hand of Darkness', 1, 1969),
  ('Things Fall Apart', 2, 1958),
  ('Kindred', 3, 1979),
  ('The Dispossessed', 1, 1974),
  ('Arrow of God', 2, 1964);

SELECT b.title, a.name AS author, b.published_year
FROM books AS b
JOIN authors AS a ON a.id = b.author_id
ORDER BY b.title;

-- Every constraint on the two tables, by the name PostgreSQL gave it
SELECT conrelid::regclass::text AS table_name, conname AS constraint_name, contype AS type
FROM pg_constraint
WHERE conrelid IN ('authors'::regclass, 'books'::regclass)
ORDER BY table_name, constraint_name;
